title: The Hollow Colony
premise: Cyrus Brightwater has spent nine years alone tending Earth's last seed vault, broadcasting a maintenance beacon no one answers—until a distress call arrives in Pre-Collapse Standard, a language dead for two centuries, from the Meridian, a generation ship whose cryosleep bays hold two rival human lineages: the colonists who fled Earth and the loyalists who exiled them. The signal's sender, an archivist named Ivo Sarn, reveals that the fleet's founding truce expires in one hundred days, and whichever lineage wakes first will inherit both the ship and the claim to reseeded Earth. As Cyrus decodes the vault's hidden origin records, she learns her own caretaker post was designed as the truce's tiebreaker—a living arbiter neither faction was supposed to control—and that her employers erased her identity to make her neutral. When the Meridian arrives and both factions attempt to seize the vault, Cyrus must choose whether to wake one half of humanity, refuse both, or forge a third inheritance: waking only the children of both lineages and forcing the adults to negotiate for them. She chooses the children, dissolving the truce into a shared custody of the future, and broadcasts the vault's beacon at last as an invitation rather than a warning.
about_author: Kestrel Dunmore is the pen name of a former archival technician who spent six years cataloguing obsolete agricultural data before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who maintain things nobody remembers needing.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Answers
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A day in the seed vault's rhythms: checking germination trays, logging frost damage, transmitting the routine beacon. Establishes her solitude, competence, and the small rituals that keep loneliness at bay. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by the question she never asks aloud—who is this beacon for?

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The vault's array catches a burst transmission; linguistic analysis flags it as Pre-Collapse Standard, extinct for two centuries. She verifies it three times before believing it. Emotional beat: vertigo—the first voice from outside in nine years, speaking a language only archives remember.

chapters.title: Ivo Sarn, Archivist
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, with recorded replies from Ivo. The sender identifies himself aboard the Meridian, a generation ship whose existence isn't in any database she can access. He asks a strange question: does the vault still have its Arbiter? Emotional beat: wary curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: What the Manifest Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV via transmission logs. He explains the Meridian's two cryosleep populations—the Exile line and the Loyalist line—and the founding truce that kept both frozen until a neutral ground could be certified. His own faction wants him silenced. Emotional beat: hope entangled with fear of what his message will cost him.

chapters.title: The Caretaker Clause
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Digging into the vault's sealed administrative layer, she finds her employment contract references a clause she never signed: designation 'Arbiter-Null,' identity redacted by her employers. Her name, history, and origins were erased before she arrived. Emotional beat: betrayal—the life she thought was hers was a constructed vacancy.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Manufactured Silence
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, flashback-heavy. She reconstructs how she was recruited, drugged, and delivered to the vault, and realizes every 'choice' she remembered was staged. Ivo confirms the same practice created the original Arbiters. Emotional beat: grief for a self that may never have existed, hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Sleepers and a Lie
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Aboard the Meridian, he smuggles records showing the truce expires in one hundred days regardless; whoever wakes first claims inheritance of Earth itself. His faction, the Archivists, believe Cyrus can certify neutrality—if she survives long enough to choose. Emotional beat: the weight of pinning everything on a stranger.

chapters.title: First Contact Protocol, Improvised
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She teaches Ivo degraded modern Standard while he coaches her through reading Pre-Collapse legal texts; their lessons become the book's first intimacy. Meanwhile the vault detects the Meridian changing course toward Earth. Emotional beat: connection across impossible distance, and dread of its ending.

chapters.title: The Vault's Second Purpose
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Deep in sublevel four she finds the vault wasn't built to preserve seeds—it was built to preserve evidence: genetic registries proving both Meridian lineages descend from the same sabotaged launch. The 'two peoples' were always one. Emotional beat: revelation that reframes the entire conflict as inherited fiction.

chapters.title: Loyalist Wake Order
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The Meridian's Loyalist faction forces an early thaw of their bay, citing truce technicalities; Ivo's transmissions go dark mid-sentence. Cyrus watches his channel flatline. Emotional beat: helplessness sharpening into decision—she can't stay invisible anymore.

chapters.title: Ninety-Nine Days
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She begins preparing the vault for arrival: arming nothing, but locking the evidence core and drafting an arbitration framework from the Pre-Collapse texts. First physical sign of the Meridian in orbit. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into methodical purpose.

chapters.title: The Landing Party
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Six Loyalists land under white flags; their commander, Wren Oduya, is courteous, exhausted, and lying about her authority. She recognizes the Arbiter protocol on sight—and offers Cyrus protection in exchange for certification. Emotional beat: charm as a weapon; Cyrus feels the trap closing gently.

chapters.title: Wren Oduya's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashbacks to waking early among frozen rivals; she believes waking her people first is mercy, since the Exiles would do worse. She genuinely likes Cyrus, which complicates everything. Emotional beat: a villain who is right about half of everything.

chapters.title: Exile Signal
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A second transmission reaches the vault—from the Exile bay, still frozen, using Ivo's stolen access codes. Their spokesperson, an elder named Tamsin Vael, makes the mirror-image argument Wren made. Emotional beat: the sickening symmetry of two justified grievances.

chapters.title: The Evidence Core
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, with Wren present. Cyrus reveals the genetic registries proving common ancestry. Wren's composure cracks—not with denial but with fury at the founders who froze her people over a lie. Emotional beat: truth offered not as victory but as wound.

chapters.title: Mutiny in the Frozen Bays
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, restored. He's alive, imprisoned in the Exile bay, and has been quietly teaching frozen-lineage crew members to wake selectively. Both factions' moderates begin covert contact through him. Emotional beat: fragile conspiracy, hope with a countdown attached.

chapters.title: Seizure
chapters.summary: Action chapter, multiple POVs. Wren's hardliners storm the vault's sublevels to destroy the evidence core; Tamsin's faction simultaneously attempts an unauthorized landing. Cyrus triggers the vault's ancient defense—not weapons, but total lockdown, sealing everyone inside together. Emotional beat: chaos forced into proximity.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Enemies trapped in the seed vault's green levels for six days: shared meals grown from the very seeds they're fighting over, arguments that become negotiations, Wren and Tamsin confronting each other across a hydroponics table. Emotional beat: hostility eroding under enforced domesticity.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She proposes her arbitration: wake only the children of both lineages—all of them, raised together on Earth under joint custody—while the adult factions remain frozen until they ratify a shared charter. The room erupts. Emotional beat: audacity; the loner demanding the impossible.

chapters.title: Vote Under Glass
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Under the vault's dome, with the evidence core broadcast on open channels, both factions vote. Wren breaks with her hardliners; Tamsin concedes the registry's truth; Ivo mediates the custody terms. It passes by eleven votes. Emotional beat: exhaustion, disbelief, the trembling aftermath of yes.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The children's bays open—one by one, forty-one kids from two supposed enemy peoples step onto Earth soil together. Wren kneels to catch the smallest; Tamsin weeps without shame; Ivo finally meets Cyrus in person. Emotional beat: release after a hundred days of held breath.

chapters.title: Invitation, Not Warning
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, final chapter. She rewrites the beacon's message from automated warning to open invitation, signs it with her chosen name—Cyrus Brightwater, self-appointed—and plants the first external seedbed with the children. The vault becomes a school. Emotional beat: an identity not recovered but authored; inheritance claimed by building something worth inheriting.
